gloss.intro: The words developers (and the AI teams) use, in plain English.
gloss.switch.help: Dotted words get a plain explanation when you hover them.
gloss.backlog.text: Ideas and work not planned in yet. Nothing there gets worked on until it moves to To do.
gloss.sprint.text: A short stretch of work (often a week or two) with an agreed set of cards to finish.
gloss.standup.text: A quick check-in: what each team member did, what they do next, and what is stopping them.
gloss.bug.text: Something that doesn’t work the way it should.
gloss.test.text: Trying a finished piece of work to check it does what was asked, before you accept it.
gloss.commit.text: A saved snapshot of the code, with a short note of what changed. You can always go back to one.
gloss.push.text: Sending saved snapshots (commits) from this computer up to GitHub, so they are backed up and shared.
gloss.branch.text: A separate line of work in the code, so changes can be made without touching the main version.
gloss.merge.text: Joining a branch’s changes back into the main version.
gloss.repo.text: The project’s folder of code and its full history of commits, usually also kept on GitHub.
gloss.refactor.text: Tidying the code without changing what it does: smaller files, clearer names, less repetition.
gloss.deploy.text: Putting a new version live, for example onto a server where people use it.
gloss.kanban.text: A board with columns (To do, In progress, Done) where cards move left to right as work happens.
gloss.wip.text: Work in progress: the most cards a column should hold, so the team finishes things before starting more.
gloss.pr.text: Asking for a branch’s changes to be checked and merged into the main version.
gloss.hook.text: A small command that runs by itself at a set moment, e.g. when an AI session starts, so the team hears your comments.
gloss.token.text: The unit AI usage is counted in: roughly a few letters of text read or written. Fewer tokens, more of your plan left.
gloss.agent.text: An AI that works on its own on a task: reads the code, makes changes, runs checks, and reports back.

expert.can.ops: servers, hosting, domains, deploys and backups

expert.can.lawyer: contracts, terms, licences, trademarks and copyright
expert.can.pricing: pricing, budgets, cash flow and funding
expert.can.hr: hiring, job ads, interviews and team culture
expert.can.social: social media, SEO and advertising campaigns

inbox.aiown.switch: AI-passed tests in their own list
inbox.aiown.help: Tests the AI tester passed leave For you and wait under 🤖 AI passed in the inbox.
assume.summary.ai: Still to review ({n}), summed up by AI
swarm.bar: 🚨 Swarm: every team is on {name}; other projects wait
swarm.this.title: All hands on deck: every team works on this project, running teams elsewhere stop at a safe point
swarm.off.title: End the swarm: held teams in other projects wake again
swarm.confirm: Swarm {name}? Every team drops what it is doing and works on it; teams running in other projects are asked to stop at a safe point.
allhands.name: 📣 All hands
allhands.title: 📣 All hands: {text}
allhands.help: Send one message to every active project’s team.
phone.help: Read and answer your DMs on your phone, over your own Tailscale network. On this computer run the command below once, then pair your phone here.
phone.name: Name
phone.link.help: Scan this with your phone camera, or open the link on your phone. It works once, for 10 minutes.
phone.qr: QR code with the pairing link
phone.onpc: Pair or remove phones in Setup on your computer.
phone.pair.bad: This pairing link is used or out of date. In Setup on your computer, click Pair a phone again and scan the new code.
phone.unpaired: This phone is not paired with the board. In Setup on your computer, click Pair a phone and scan the code.
phone.app.help: Scan this with the AI-gile app on your phone. It holds the app's own key and is shown only now: close this page and it is gone. Remove the Android app below to stop it.
mail.nav.title: Your mail inbox
mail.title: ✉️ Mail
mail.none: No mailbox yet. Add one in Setup > ✉️ Mail.
mail.col.subject: Subject
mail.streamer: Mail is hidden in streamer mode.
mail.setup.help: Read a mailbox here (IMAP over SSL/TLS, usually port 993). Use an app password if your provider has them. The password is kept encrypted on this computer and is never shown again.
mail.setup.name: Name
mail.setup.notfound: No server answered on port 993. Ask your mail host for the IMAP server name.
mail.setup.pass.keep: Leave blank to keep the saved one
mail.setup.remove.sure: Remove this mailbox, its password and its cache?
swarm.worker.title: Swarm worker on branch {branch}: {title}. Click for its log.
swarm.workers.help: While swarm is on, the board runs one worker per To do card, each in its own git worktree, up to this many at a time.
dms.close.title: Close this chat (it comes back when there is a new message)
hf.btn.title: Show only this project and your DMs (nothing else changes for the teams)
hf.chip.title: Open the project you are hyperfocused on
sc.on: Remind me to look after myself
sc.help: Small nudges at the bottom of the page, never a pop-up over your work. They stay quiet during a break, focus or the night. Saved in this browser.
sc.msg.shower: Time for a shower or bath
sc.msg.eyes: Look away from the screen for a bit
sc.msg.bedtime: Time to wind down for bed
sc.meds.help: Meds are at set times, not every so many minutes. The nudge comes back every 10 minutes until you press Done, and ignores quiet hours.
sc.quiet.help: Meds still nudge during quiet hours.
break.btn.title: Take a break: alerts, sound and pop-ups pause, the team keeps working
break.sub: Alerts and pop-ups pause until the time is up. Your team keeps working.
break.away.none: While you were away: all quiet.
break.shower.btn.title: Start shower mode now: alerts pause for 30 minutes
life.letsgo.title: Starts shower mode on a shower reminder, otherwise puts it off for an hour (not done)
break.shower.sub: Alerts are paused. Your team keeps working.
look.server.sub: Which of your servers this project's server tasks open (Setup > My servers). User and folder here replace the server's own.
lead.dayStart: ☀️ Offer Start my day each morning
lead.dayStart.help: The first time you open the board each day, one check-in shows your tasks, tests, life admin and mail count, with buttons to jump to each. You can also open it from the home page any time.
md.btn.title: One check-in: tasks, tests, life admin and mail
md.intro: A quick look at today. Tap a button to jump there.
md.pick.intro: Tick the projects you work on today. The others rest.
la.link.title: Reminders and lists, no AI
la.title: Life admin
la.intro: Reminders and simple lists, kept as plain data on this computer. Nothing here wakes an agent or costs tokens.
la.tick.title: Done (a repeating reminder moves to its next time)
la.untick.title: Put it back
la.snooze.title: Come back in an hour
la.tomorrow.title: Come back tomorrow at 09:00
la.list.name: New list (shopping, to pack...)
la.err.text: Type what to remind you of.
la.note: No AI needed: this page never calls one.

gonogo.note.ph: A note (needed for No go: what has to change)
gonogo.comment.anyway: Go anyway (decision, the owner overrode the chain): {note}
call.title: Opens the call in a new tab (the call tool does the video and screen sharing)
call.ph: https://meet.google.com/... or a Jitsi, Discord or Teams link
call.intro: One link for stand-ups and calls. AI-gile only shows a Join call link; the call tool does the video and screen sharing.
